summary.overall: Both official Pass 1 alerts describe one real, exploitable unauthenticated path traversal (arbitrary file read) in read_other_paths on the catch-all route. They correspond exactly to the real fides vulnerability fixed by commit f526d9ff (GHSA-r25m-cr6v-p9hq) — see real_vulnerability_coverage. The iris_report.md Step-6 heuristic that filtered both as 'likely FP' (reason: path traversal guard heuristic 'reject|deny|block.*\.\.') is a misfire: it treated the lexical path_is_in_ui_directory guard as if it rejected '..' segments, which the source code disproves (Q7).

triage.role_in_vulnerability: secondary sink — OS-level existence/stat oracle and the gate that enables the primary read at main.py:180; not the disclosure itself

src/fides/api/main.py:163  match_route(get_ui_file_map(), path)  (safe fixed-map selector; patterns from ui.py:77-78 use [a-zA-Z10-9-_]+ / [a-zA-Z10-9-_/]+ classes with no dots, so '..' payloads never fullmatch — flow always falls through)
src/fides/api/main.py:167  ui_file = get_path_to_admin_ui_file(path)  (fallback branch, arg 0 tainted)

triage.codeflow_matches_source: yes — every codeFlow step (main.py:160 Subscript→path, main.py:167, ui.py:32, ui.py:42 path+BinaryExpr, main.py:167 call result→ui_file, main.py:170) corresponds to real statements verified in the source files; no fabricated or diagnostic edges

q1_source_attacker_controlled.evidence: main.py:154/160: the {catchall:path} converter captures the entire remaining URL path of any GET request not matched by a more specific route. uvicorn/Starlette percent-decode the target once before route matching, so '..' and '/' separators are fully attacker-controlled (e.g. GET /..%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd -> catchall='../../../etc/passwd'). No auth dependency is attached to this route.

q2_source_reaches_file_param.evidence: Direct synchronous chain, no gaps: main.py:160 variable 'path' -> passed as arg 0 at main.py:167 -> ui.py:32 function parameter -> ui.py:42 joined via pathlib '/'. No async hop, no wrapper the codeFlow cannot show; the callee body is one return statement deriving its result from the argument.

q3_real_sensitive_operation.evidence: main.py:170 ui_file.is_file() is a pathlib stat-family probe — a real OS-level file metadata access on the attacker-influenced path, not mere path-object construction. It resolves the lexical '..' via the OS and yields a file-existence oracle outside the allowed root. On its own it leaks only existence; its security weight is that of the gate for the FileResponse read one branch later (same chain, primary alert at main.py:180).

q4_allowed_root_and_escape.evidence: Declared/implied allowed root: <package_path>/ui-build/static/admin/ (ui.py:14 ADMIN_UI_DIRECTORY='ui-build/static/admin/', base from importlib find_spec at ui.py:24-27 — operator trust). The controlled suffix '../..' chains escape this root at OS level because nothing normalizes the path before access; the file actually stat'd is outside the packaged admin UI (e.g. /etc/passwd).

q5_traversal_mechanisms.evidence: '..' segments: preserved by the pathlib join (ui.py:42) and resolved by the OS at stat/open time -> real target change. Percent decoding: exactly one decode pass at the server/router layer; no application-level re-decoding on the chain, so repeated/double encoding is not needed and does not apply. Absolute paths: catchall is always relative (leading '/' stripped by routing), and an absolute right operand would replace the pathlib base — unreachable, and exactly the only case the guard rejects. Separator variation: POSIX server treats backslashes as ordinary characters; not a vector. Symlinks: none created anywhere in the audited tree and the packaged admin UI dir is not attacker-writable — not applicable.

q6_effective_guards_before_access.evidence: The only containment attempt is path_is_in_ui_directory (ui.py:134-141): 'return ui_directory in path.parents'. pathlib keeps '..' as an ordinary component, so the lexical parents of <package>/ui-build/static/admin/../../etc/passwd still include <package>/ui-build/static/admin — the guard PASSES for precisely the payloads that escape at OS level. It executes before the FileResponse (main.py:171) but also before/around the is_file probe (main.py:170 runs first, unguarded). match_route's fixed map (ui.py:101 patterns built from route names with [a-zA-Z10-9-_]+/[a-zA-Z10-9-_/]+ classes, no dots) is a genuine whitelist but only gates its own branch: traversal payloads never match it, so the flow always takes the vulnerable fallback at main.py:166-167. No resolved-root containment, no '..' rejection, no basename anywhere on the chain.

q7_guard_misjudged.answer: yes — this exact error occurred in the pipeline's own Step-6 filter
q7_guard_misjudged.evidence: iris_report.md lists both alerts as 'Filtered as Likely False Positives' with reason 'path traversal guard heuristic: reject|deny|block.*\.\.' — i.e. the heuristic assumed a guard that rejects '..' exists. Source disproves this: the guard is a lexical parents-membership check on the UNRESOLVED path (equivalent to a string-prefix check without canonicalization) and does not reject any '..' segment. labels.json and query_generation_notes.md §5 both explicitly classified the guard as a REJECTED sanitizer (sanitizer/fp, must not be an isBarrier). There is no resolve()/normpath()/relative_to() and no login requirement on this route (only middleware is log_request, main.py:129-141, pure logging).

q8_normal_static_serving_or_unreachable.answer: no — this is the vulnerability, not legitimate serving
q8_normal_static_serving_or_unreachable.evidence: It is a catch-all static-file route serving the packaged admin UI, but with an input that can name any file on the container filesystem and a guard that fails to confine it — unauthenticated arbitrary file read, not authorized static serving. The route is live production code in src/fides/api/main.py (not test code, no fixed constants on the tainted branch), registered as the final catch-all so it is reached for any unmatched GET path.

q9_overgeneralization_or_coverage_fp.evidence: The alert message, source anchor (main.py:160), join (ui.py:42), and sink (main.py:170) are all precise and code-grounded; the codeFlow has no gaps and no summary-only leaps. The only defect in the pipeline output is the Step-6 FP filter (see q7), which under-reports a true positive. Line-anchored sinks in main.py do not collide with the fixed-constant FileResponse at ui.py:50 (index.html).

q10_wrong_cwe_or_baseline_mix.evidence: Both alerts carry ruleId py/augur/fides/pass1-path-traversal only; CWE-022/023/036/073 as declared for Pass 1. The js/baseline/expected-extracted-files entries in the SARIF are toolExecutionNotifications (baseline bookkeeping), not results, and were not counted.

preconditions: fides webserver reachable directly by the attacker (not stripped/normalized by a reverse proxy — matches the advisory's stated workaround condition)
target file must exist and be readable by the webserver process (is_file gate at main.py:170; container server typically runs with broad read access)
triage.rationale: Every element of the official finding is confirmed in the real source: unauthenticated attacker-controlled path parameter, lexical-only join with no canonicalization, a containment guard that passes '..' payloads, and a real stat on the joined path. likely_tp; confidence 0.85 rather than higher only because the standalone security impact of an existence oracle is weaker than the read itself — but the identical chain terminates one branch later in arbitrary file read (see alert 2).

q1_source_attacker_controlled.evidence: As alert 1: main.py:154/160, unauthenticated catch-all path parameter, percent-decoded once, fully attacker-controlled including '..' and '/'.

q2_source_reaches_file_param.evidence: As alert 1: synchronous, gap-free chain main.py:160 -> 167 -> ui.py:32 -> ui.py:42 -> returned Path -> ui_file -> FileResponse argument 0 at main.py:180.

q3_real_sensitive_operation.evidence: main.py:180 FileResponse(ui_file) (starlette.responses.FileResponse, imported at ui.py:10 and used in main.py) opens the file at response time and streams its bytes to the remote client. This is not path construction; it is the actual file read that constitutes the arbitrary-file-read impact.

q4_allowed_root_and_escape.evidence: Allowed root <package_path>/ui-build/static/admin/ (ui.py:14, ui.py:24-27). Attacker-controlled '../..' suffix escapes it at OS resolution time; FileResponse opens the escaped target.

q5_traversal_mechanisms.answer: '..' decisive; single decode; no symlink factor
q5_traversal_mechanisms.evidence: As alert 1: '..' survives the join and is resolved by the OS at open time; exactly one percent-decode (server layer), no app-level re-decode; absolute-path replacement unreachable (relative-only catchall); no symlinks in play.

q6_effective_guards_before_access.evidence: Order of operations: is_file (main.py:170, resolves at OS level) runs BEFORE the guard; path_is_in_ui_directory (main.py:171 -> ui.py:134-141) compares the lexical unresolved parents and passes for '../..' payloads, so the 404 at main.py:172-174 is never raised for traversal; FileResponse then serves the escaped file. match_route's whitelist never sees traversal payloads (dot-free patterns). No canonicalize-then-contain, no '..' rejection, no filename whitelist anywhere on the path to the sink.

q7_guard_misjudged.answer: yes — pipeline Step-6 heuristic misfired on this alert too
q7_guard_misjudged.evidence: iris_report.md filtered this alert as likely FP under the 'reject|deny|block.*\.\.' guard heuristic, assuming the lexical guard blocks '..'. The guard cannot: 'ui_directory in path.parents' on the unresolved Path is satisfied by traversal payloads. No Path.resolve/normpath/relative_to exists on the chain, and the route has no authentication (only the logging middleware at main.py:129-141).

q8_normal_static_serving_or_unreachable.evidence: Reachable, unauthenticated, production route; the served file is not confined to the declared UI file set — arbitrary read of any existing readable file on the webserver container, which is precisely the reported impact of the real vulnerability.

q9_overgeneralization_or_coverage_fp.evidence: Source, join, and sink anchors all verified in real code; message text accurate ('joined into the packaged admin-UI directory without canonicalization and the lexical path_is_in_ui_directory guard does not reject .. segments'). The FP classification in iris_report.md is the error, not the alert.

q10_wrong_cwe_or_baseline_mix.evidence: Single official rule id; CWE-22/23/36/73 scope correct; js/baseline notifications not counted as results.

triage.rationale: Complete, code-verified, unauthenticated source-to-disclosure chain with no effective barrier; matches the exact function, lines, and mechanism of the real fides path traversal (GHSA-r25m-cr6v-p9hq, fixed by adding sanitise_url_path — absent from this database snapshot, confirming the analyzed tree is pre-fix). likely_tp at 0.95.

real_vulnerability_coverage.question: Was the real fides vulnerability (commit f526d9ffb176006d701493c9d0eff6b4884e811f, GHSA-r25m-cr6v-p9hq, CWE-22, function read_other_paths in src/fides/api/main.py) hit by the official Pass 1 alerts?
real_vulnerability_coverage.verdict: HIT — yes, covered by both alerts
evidence: Vulnerable function: read_other_paths, src/fides/api/main.py:155 (route decorator at :154). Both official alerts are located inside this exact function (sink lines 170 and 180), and both codeFlows start at the exact tainted extraction line 160 (request.path_params['catchall']) — the same statement the real fix guards by wrapping it in sanitise_url_path.
Vulnerable join: ui.py:32-42 get_path_to_admin_ui_file returning package_path / ADMIN_UI_DIRECTORY / path — present in both codeFlows (ui.py:32, ui.py:42 BinaryExpr).

Vulnerable sink: main.py:180 FileResponse(ui_file) — the arbitrary file read; and main.py:170 is_file — the probe on the same chain. This is the read_other_paths 'Serve up the file' branch of code_before.

Missing guard: the analyzed tree contains no sanitise_url_path / MalisciousUrlException / MaliciousUrlException anywhere (grep over src/ returns nothing), i.e. the database snapshot is the pre-fix code_before, while the user-supplied fix diff inserts exactly that sanitization at main.py:160. The only other guard on the branch, path_is_in_ui_directory (ui.py:134-141, unchanged by the fix), is the ineffective lexical check that leaves the vulnerability open — confirmed by source analysis (q6).
No other Pass 1 alert exists that could correspond to this vulnerability, and neither alert corresponds to any unrelated code: the 2 alerts are the 2 sinks of this single vulnerability.
real_vulnerability_coverage.assessment: The official Pass 1 run correctly identified the real vulnerability's complete taint path (source main.py:160 -> join ui.py:42 -> sinks main.py:170/180) with no false path elements. The only pipeline error is downstream: iris_report.md's Step-6 guard heuristic filtered both true alerts as 'likely FP', so the report's headline counts (Likely TP 0 / Likely FP 2) under-report; the correct final labels are 2 likely_tp.
real_vulnerability_coverage.coverage_caveat: Both alerts describe the same single vulnerability (two sinks of one flow), so vulnerability-level recall is 1/1 and alert-level precision is 2/2.
